packages.label: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְקוֹם גְּנִיזַת הַצַּדִּיק
packages.label_en: Eretz Yisrael and the Tzaddik's Burial Place
packages.reason: These concepts share the same essential nature: the domain of the holy land and its spiritual reality as expressed in the burial place of the true tzaddik. The Rebbe states that the burial place of true tzaddikim IS holy with the actual holiness of Eretz Yisrael itself ('מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ'). This is a bechina relationship: the burial place and Eretz Yisrael are two expressions of the same holiness. The tzaddikim are the ones through whom this identity is realized — they are the ones who 'inherit' Eretz Yisrael through the transference of its holiness to their burial place. Thus ארץ ישראל, מקום גניזת הצדיק, and קדושת ארץ ישראל all belong to one domain: the living reality of the holy land, which is not merely a geographical location but a quality of holiness that true tzaddikim carry with them even in death.

merge_notes.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that the burial place of true tzaddikim IS Eretz Yisrael in holiness — 'מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ'. The word 'ממש' (literally/actually) underscores that this is not metaphorical equivalence but an identity of essential nature. This is an unambiguous bechina.

The Rebbe frames the tzaddikim's inheritance as acquiring the specific holiness-quality of Eretz Yisrael. The holiness of Eretz Yisrael is not a separate concept from Eretz Yisrael itself — it is its essential nature. Both belong in the same package as different faces of the same holy-land reality.

The tzaddik and his burial place are inseparable in this Torah: it is specifically the 'true tzaddik' whose burial place acquires the holiness of Eretz Yisrael. The tzaddik is the agent through whom the identity of burial place with Eretz Yisrael is actualized. They belong to the same domain of holy-land identity.
